faq.a: Short how-tos for one seller job each. They cover a phone photo, a plain main image, a first video ad, the frame each app wants, and a fair test of versions.

faq.q: How does a guide become a file?
faq.a: You follow the steps, upload your product photo or paste the product page, and make the file on the tool that guide names. The guide is the plan. The tool makes the file.

faq.q: Why read a guide instead of hiring someone to film?
faq.a: A lunch-container photo on the kitchen table is enough to start the phone-photo guide after you close. Hiring someone to film that container means waiting on their calendar. The guide uses the picture you can take yourself.
Someone packing orders who has never booked a studio. A marketer can use the same pages when a client needs a file this week. A shop with a full photo team can skip them.

faq.q: Can I follow them if I have never edited video?
faq.a: Yes. You need a phone photo, not a timeline. The first-ad guide stops at a file you can post. Setting up the ad account stays in that app's own help.

faq.q: Which kinds of shops are they for?
faq.a: The photo steps and the video steps are the same kind of task for every shop. Rules differ by product type, so check the [page for your kind of shop](page:industries) before you upload.

faq.q: Can one phone photo feed every guide?
faq.a: Yes, if it shows the whole item clearly. A still and a clip made from it are separate files, each with its own credit cost.

faq.q: Where can I post the file?
faq.a: Wherever the guide's shape fits. A tall file is the phone placement. A square sits in a feed. The [platform pages](page:platforms) name the usual frames. Your own store can use the download too.

faq.q: How much do the files cost?
faq.a: A product photo is 24 credits. A clip is 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. The cost shows before you start. If a file does not finish, its credits come back.

faq.q: Can I sell with the file?
faq.a: Yes. Use it in ads and on your store. The download has no watermark.

faq.q: Which guide makes a video with a person and a voice?
faq.a: The first-ad guide does, when you want a person on screen. You can also keep the frame on the product and still have a spoken line. The photo guides stop at a still.

faq.q: Can I create a video without a template?
faq.a: The guide names the one task, the file you should end with, and the checks to make before you spend credits on a second try.
